title: Kullback–Leibler divergence between probability mass functions
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite discrete measurable space, and let $p$ and $q$ be probability mass functions on $\Omega$, each regarded as the probability measure it induces. Then the Kullback–Leibler divergence $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p \,\|\, q)$, valued in $[0,\infty]$, equals $+\infty$ whenever there exists some $\omega \in \Omega$ with $q(\omega) = 0$ and $p(\omega) \neq 0$, and otherwise equals the value in $[0,\infty]$ obtained from
\[
  \sum_{\omega \in \Omega} p(\omega)\,\log\!\frac{p(\omega)}{q(\omega)},
\]
where each mass $p(\omega)$, $q(\omega)$ is taken as its real value and negative sums are read as $0$.
hypotheses_covered: Ω is a finite discrete measurable space
p and q are probability mass functions on Ω
case split on whether some ω has q(ω)=0 and p(ω)≠0
